scores.reason: Two guidelines (Endocrine Society 2009, ENETS 2016) recommend insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin and BOHB at documented hypoglycaemia; the guideline grades the evidence low or very low, and no randomised or outcome study of measurement-guided care was found. Scored 3 as guideline-backed consensus, at the lower edge.

scores.reason: Glucose, imaging and clinical features cannot show endogenous hyperinsulinism; insulin plus C-peptide at hypoglycaemia is the only biochemical test that does (proinsulin and BOHB are adjuncts). Judged from the mechanism and guideline logic, not from a reclassification rate (rule 19 would cap at 2 on mechanism alone; 4 chosen because no alternative exists, see anchor_issues).

scores.reason: PES 2015 and Endocrine Society 2009 endorse the insulin-high, C-peptide-suppressed pattern, but sensitivity and specificity of the pattern were not retrieved; the evidence is mechanistic plus case reports. Cohort accuracy data not found in the screened records.

scores.reason: The pattern separates exogenous from endogenous hyperinsulinism where drug screen, insulin analogue-specific LC-MS/MS or antibody tests are alternatives and are partly needed because immunoassays can miss analogues. No data showing the measurement changes the answer given those alternatives; mechanism only, so 2.

The international HI guideline (Rec 1.4, Grade 1, low-quality evidence) applies the adult-style insulin and C-peptide work-up to children older than 2 years; the child-specific evidence is small surgical series (title only), so the support is extrapolated adult consensus.

scores.reason: Biochemical proof of hyperinsulinism has no imaging or genetic substitute and, with MEN1 clues, directs the path away from congenital HI work-up. No reclassification data; 3 rests on guideline text that makes the test the entry step. Confidence low because this is not an accuracy comparison.

scores.reason: ENETS 2016 endorses calcium-stimulated hepatic venous insulin sampling (positive 90-100%) from two small series; a later 80-patient surgical cohort found arterial stimulation venous sampling sensitivity 65% (n=20) and percutaneous transhepatic sampling 90% (n=10), so accuracy is variable and observational only.
sources: PMID 26742109 full text per project file usecases-verified.md row 22

scores.reason: Useful in the defined subgroup with negative imaging: in the 80-patient series invasive methods localised the tumour in 7 of 7 patients with 14 non-visualised tumours that had them. No head-to-head against newer imaging (for example exendin PET) was screened.

Observational accuracy only: a 37-case, 42-control study gave AUC 0.97, sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 95.2% for OGTT insulin and C-peptide ratios; a systematic review found two case-control studies (106 patients) at risk of bias. ENETS quotes single-centre data. Cases were confirmed insulinoma, so applicability to fast-negative patients is untested.

scores.reason: Useful in the defined subgroup where the fast is negative or not feasible; alternatives are an extended or mixed-meal test. The studies used the 72-hour fast as the reference, not fast-negative patients, so added value in that subgroup is not shown.
scores.correction: 2026-10-23, main session, after skeptic V13: PMID 42221390 found no difference in insulin or C-peptide AUC between insulinoma and reactive hypoglycaemia; glucose alone separated them

scores.reason: The FDA label sets peak stimulated C-peptide >=0.2 pmol/mL on MMTT (plus an islet autoantibody) as an eligibility criterion; approval rests on a surrogate (C-peptide decline at week 78). In PROTECT, 217 vs 111 patients, difference 0.13 pmol/mL (95% CI 0.09-0.17); 94.9% vs 79.2% kept peak C-peptide >=0.2. Surrogate approval scores 3 (clarification 9). Selection by C-peptide was not itself randomised (clarification 8 would cap at 2; see anchor_issues).
sources: FDA Tzield label rev 06/2026 s2.1, s14.2 per project file usecases-verified.md row 29
scores.correction: 2026-10-23, main session, after skeptic V13: rule 8; PROTECT used C-peptide as the efficacy endpoint and never tested selection by C-peptide

scores.reason: Stimulated C-peptide identifies residual beta-cell function; alternatives are autoantibodies (also required) and time since diagnosis. No retrieved analysis shows C-peptide selection improves outcome beyond those, so mechanism only, 2.
sources: FDA Tzield label per project file

scores.reason: Three small single-centre cohorts with ROC accuracy: UCPCR >=0.7 nmol/mmol, sensitivity 100% (95% CI 92-100), specificity 97% (91-99), n=264 after 2 years; UCPCR >=0.22, AUC 0.93, n=69; UCPCR >=0.28, sensitivity 97%, specificity 88%, n=80. Cutoffs differ 3-fold, each data-derived and not externally validated. No outcome or management study.

Defined subgroup (diabetes >2 years, antibody status unclear) where clinical features misclassify; genetic testing and autoantibodies are alternatives and the abstracts report no comparison or incremental AUC against them. Fasting C-peptide did worse than UCPCR in one cohort (sensitivity 63%).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A prospective accuracy study with a standard assay-specific cutoff set (current insulin and C-peptide immunoassays) in consecutive patients with Whipple's triad.
path_to_viability.basis: Thresholds are second-hand and the guideline grades the evidence low or very low (PMID 19088155).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Report analogue cross-reactivity per assay with a validated cutoff pattern, and a cohort accuracy study of insulin plus C-peptide against drug screen or LC-MS/MS.
path_to_viability.basis: Immunoassays vary in analogue detection (PMID 39086570, 39030378, 36733550 titles only); no cohort accuracy found.

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A paediatric series of insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia in children over 2 years with confirmed insulinoma or MEN1, with age-specific cutoffs.
path_to_viability.basis: The guideline recommendation is Grade 1 on low-quality evidence (PMID 37454648).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A head-to-head cohort of calcium-stimulated venous sampling against exendin PET/CT in negative-imaging patients, with surgical cure as the outcome.
path_to_viability.basis: Evidence is small series; sensitivity ranged 65-100% (PMID 31369096, ENETS 2016).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A prospective study of OGTT or mixed-meal insulin and C-peptide ratios in patients with postprandial symptoms and a negative fast, with an external validation cohort.
path_to_viability.basis: Existing models were fit on confirmed cases versus controls, n=37/42 (PMID 32529519), and the systematic review judged them at risk of bias (PMID 38863915).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: Clinical-outcome follow-up of PROTECT (HbA1c, insulin dose, hypoglycaemia) and a subgroup analysis by baseline C-peptide showing selection adds to antibody status.
path_to_viability.basis: Approval is on a surrogate; ADA 2026 does not endorse the stage 3 indication (project file row 29).

path_to_viability.missing_piece: A multi-centre validation of a single UCPCR cutoff against genetic and autoantibody-defined type, with a comparison to autoantibody testing alone.
path_to_viability.basis: Three single-centre cohorts with cutoffs 0.22 to 0.7 (PMID 23289766, 25792383, 32052124).

anchor_issues: Row 1 D8: rule 19 says mechanism alone scores at most 2, but the anchor for 4 is 'no alternative'. I scored 4 because no alternative test shows endogenous hyperinsulinism; a reader applying rule 19 strictly would give 2 or 3.

Row 29 D2: anchor 9 (surrogate approval = 3) and clarification 8 (entry criterion without testing measurement-guided selection = 2 at most) conflict, because the label makes the C-peptide threshold a regulatory eligibility criterion. I chose 3 (anchor 9, regulatory status).

Row 2 and 22: the measure is a secretion pattern or a vein gradient, not an IR index; D8 compares against drug or localisation alternatives, which the anchor allows but was written for clinical-feature alternatives.
Row 1 D2: guideline-backed consensus on low-quality evidence is scored 3 by the anchor wording; I would call it a weak 3.
assumptions: Searches shared across rows (same evidence base); at most 6 searches in total, below the 6-per-row cap.

Measure types: rows 1, 2, 23, 24 are insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia or post-load (23 post-load, ratios); row 22 hepatic venous insulin after calcium; rows 29 and 33 are C-peptide (stimulated MMTT; urinary post-meal ratio). None is an insulin-resistance index.
